_comment: Single source of truth for the unified gateway: which upstream serves which
model, and whether that upstream needs the agentrouter filter.
The gateway's /u route dispatches on the request's `model` field, so a client
only needs ONE provider entry (http://127.0.0.1:7878/u/v1) and picks a model.
tools/build-model-catalog.cjs reads this file, so the codex picker and the
gateway can never disagree about which models exist.
`wire`: responses = upstream speaks the Responses API natively (pass through);
chat      = upstream is chat/completions only (the gateway bridges).
`filter`: run filter.mjs (char allowlist + word list + identity rewrite).
Only agentrouter needs it; on other upstreams it only loses fidelity.
`proxy`: CONNECT tunnel, needed by anyrouter.top (TLS-blocked when direct).

_strictItemIds_comment: ps.air-outer.com validates the PREFIX of every REPLAYED item id against the
item type, and answers 400 when it does not match:
reasoning -> rs, message -> msg, function_call / function_call_output -> fc,
web_search_call -> ws, custom_tool_call -> ctc, custom_tool_call_output -> ctco.
A session previously served by relaycat (which mints ids as `item_...`) replayed
those ids here verbatim and died on:
Renaming cannot fix it: the id is resolved in the upstream's own store, and a
rewritten one comes back as 'Item with id ... not found'. So the gateway DROPS an
id whose prefix contradicts the contract, and additionally retries with ALL ids
dropped only when the upstream itself rejects a replay. Class implementation and
Only this provider sets the flag. Every other upstream keeps its own ids - the
gateway must not rewrite what it has no evidence about.

relaycat65._comment:
relaycat, SECOND key - same host, cheaper group: 0.065x vs the 0.2x of the
`relaycat` entry. Kept separate because providers.json selects a key per
provider; the two keys see different model sets and different prices.

MODEL OVERLAP: this key's group lists 18 ids, of which 6 serve. The 0.2x key
lists 27 and serves 6, and the SERVING SETS OVERLAP on gpt-5.6-sol,
gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.5 and codex-auto-review. Those ids are
therefore registered under BOTH providers, and the display name carries the
ratio so the cheaper one is obvious when picking.

THIS KEY'S EXCLUSIVE: gpt-6-sol, which is the reason to use it - it accepts
reasoning effort `xhigh` (probed 200) and the xhigh run really does more work
(33s vs 1.5s at low/high/max), so it is not being silently downgraded.

DEAD IDS (502/503 on probe, deliberately NOT registered): gpt-5.2,
gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5.3-codex-spark, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.6-luna,
gpt-5.5-openai-compact, gpt-5.6-sol-openai-compact,
gpt-5.6-terra-openai-compact. The three gpt-image-* ids are image models and
were not probed.

gpt-6.1-sol DOES NOT EXIST on this key: /v1/models omits it and a direct call
answers 404 (a real not-found, not a channel problem). The newest id here is
gpt-6-sol.

antigravity._comment:
antigravity-tools (Antigravity Manager), a LOCAL proxy on 127.0.0.1:8045 that
fronts Google's Antigravity/Gemini Code Assist backends. Not a remote relay:
it is a desktop app the user runs, with its own account pool.

WIRE: responses is native. /v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions and
/v1/messages all exist. No proxy needed (the app dials upstream itself).

GEMINI IS GEO-BLOCKED, CLAUDE IS NOT - measured 2026-09-30, and this is the
single most important fact about this provider:
  claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, claude-sonnet-4-5,
  claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5          -> HTTP 200
  gemini-3.8-flash (and every variant), gemini-3-pro-high, gemini-3.1-pro,
  gemini-2.5-flash                             -> HTTP 400
        'User location is not supported for the API use.'
  gemini-2.5-pro, gpt-4o                       -> HTTP 403
        'Verify your account to continue.'
So ONLY the Claude ids are registered. Do not add a gemini id here until a
probe returns 200 - the request never leaves the account's region for those.

WHY the block: the app's business requests do NOT go through the configured
upstream proxy. Measured: `proxy.upstream_proxy` points at
http://127.0.0.1:7897 and that proxy works (exit 66.90.99.58, Tokyo JP), but
the antigravity-tools process holds ZERO connections to it. Its own update
checker DOES use the proxy, so the config is read - the model traffic just
takes a different path. Fixing that is an app-side setting, not ours.

ACCOUNT NOTE: the app's pool has two Google accounts; one is flagged
`proxy_disabled: true` and the other answers 403 'Verify your account'.
Both states are visible in its own logs. Neither is ours to change.

ovoapi._comment:
ovoapi - 'AI站长 / OVO API', a New-API relay (v1.0.0-rc.33-ovo.20260928).

HOST: the public site is https://ovoapi.site, but that site's own /api/status
api_info block names the API host as https://api-console.182yc.xyz/v1. Both
domains answer; the console host is used here because that is what the operator
publishes to clients.

WIRE: responses. Probed 2026-09-30 - /v1/responses 200, /v1/messages 200 (the
site also offers an anthropic face), /v1/chat/completions 200. Native responses
means PASSTHROUGH: no chat bridge, no filter (this provider does not need the
agentrouter character/word rules).

MODEL COVERAGE IS ONE, and that is measured, not assumed. The key's group lists
five ids, but only gpt-5.6-sol serves: three rounds x five ids gave gpt-5.6-sol
9/9 HTTP 200 while gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-astra and gpt-6-sol answered
503 'Service temporarily unavailable' on every single attempt. The dead four are
deliberately NOT registered - they would appear in the picker and never answer.
Re-probe before adding them; the announcement feed shows this operator rotates
groups often (0.055x, 0.15x, 'no-degradation' groups all advertised in late Sept).

ID HYGIENE: this upstream MINTS `item_...` ids - a function_call came back as
id=item_9d67781de5d75e3c28e3535f, the same shape relaycat uses. Unlike
agentrouter (see strictItemIds) it ACCEPTS foreign ids: replaying agentrouter's
`rs_`/`msg_` and relaycat's `item_` items in a follow-up turn all answered 200.
So this route must NOT set strictItemIds.

TOOL CALLS work on the responses face: a forced exec_command returned a proper
function_call with arguments {"cmd":"echo hi"}, and stream=true returned a
complete SSE run ending in response.completed.

ovoapi-amz._comment:
The SECOND ovoapi key - same host, DIFFERENT group, entirely different pool.

Why a separate provider instead of one entry with two keys: providers.json
selects a key per PROVIDER (keyEnv), not per model, and the two keys' model
sets do not overlap at all. OVOAPI_API_KEY serves gpt-5.6-sol; this one
serves seven Claude ids and none of the GPT ones. Merging would make one of
the two pools unreachable.

WIRE: responses, native (passthrough). All three faces answered 200 on every
id: /v1/responses, /v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions. No proxy needed.

ID HYGIENE: this pool mints `tooluse_...` ids - a THIRD shape, distinct from
agentrouter's rs_/msg_/fc_ and relaycat's item_. It ACCEPTS foreign ids:
replaying agentrouter's and relaycat's items in a follow-up turn all answered
200. So strictItemIds must stay OFF here too.

STABILITY: three rounds x seven ids, all 21 probes HTTP 200 - no intermittent
503s like the sibling key's dead GPT ids. Re-probe before trusting this for
anything long-running; the operator rotates groups often.

NOTE: claude-opus-4-8 and claude-opus-4.8 are BOTH real, distinct ids in this
pool (dash vs dot) and both serve. They are registered separately rather than
guessed to be aliases - nothing in the API says they are the same model.

_models_comment: key   = the model id the CLIENT sends (also the codex catalog slug)
value = { p: provider, m: upstream model id (omit when identical) }
Only ids that were probed live are listed. Entries whose upstream currently
answers 402/503 stay listed when the id is real (it recovers); the gateway
passes the upstream error through unchanged so the cause stays visible.

_fallback_comment: Cross-realm fallback: when the global pool answers 429/503 for this model
(i.e. every global account is cooling down), the gateway retries the SAME
request against the CN pool instead of failing the client turn.
Why CN is the fallback and not the other way round: global accounts refill
every day, while CN credits are the scarce, hard-to-regenerate resource.
So we spend global by default and only touch CN when global is exhausted.
never inferred from /status healthy counts - the pool has an all-cooling
fallback that keeps soft-cooled accounts selectable, so a healthy=0 domain

models._builtin_comment: codex built-in slugs, served natively by relaycat
models._anyrouter_claude_comment:
anyrouter exposes its claude ids ONLY on the anthropic /v1/messages face.
Probed 2026-09-24: /v1/responses answers 404 "当前 API 不支持所选模型" for every
claude id (and for gpt-5-codex / gemini-2.5-pro too - that face serves nothing),
while /v1/messages reaches the business layer. Hence the per-model
"wire": "anthropic" override (the provider default stays "responses" so
gpt-6-astra-an is unaffected).

anthropic-beta is REQUIRED. Without it the upstream answers 400 "1m 上下文已经
全量可用,请启用 1m 上下文后重试"; with it the error layer advances to 503
Service Unavailable. That 503 is a SITE-WIDE condition, not a model fault:
claude-opus-4-7 / claude-sonnet-4-5 / claude-3-5-sonnet all answered 503 at the
same moment. So these two ids are registered and routable but NOT currently
working - do not report them as available until the upstream channel pool
recovers. Verify with:
  curl -sS -o NUL -w '%{http_code}' -x http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
    -X POST https://anyrouter.top/v1/messages \
    -H 'x-api-key: <ANYROUTER_API_KEY>' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: context-1m-2025-08-07' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
  # 400 = beta header missing/wrong; 503 = header accepted, channel pool down;
  # 200 = recovered.
models._spacebunny_comment:
space-bunny-free on the opencode zen free tier. Probed 2026-09-24: HTTP 200,
tool calls work, and it is reached through the same local reverse proxy as the
other zen free models (oc-zen-proxy.mjs, port 7901), which supplies the OpenCode
client fingerprint the free tier requires.

The explicit `efforts` list is what keeps it from inheriting the provider window:
providerFor() prefers a model-level list over the provider-level one (model >
provider > null). The provider-level [low,medium,high] exists for
mimo-v2.6-flash-free, which rejects xhigh/max with a 400. A DIRECT probe of the
zen proxy (bypassing the gateway, 2026-09-24) returned 200 for every level -
minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max - so inheriting that list silently downgraded a
caller's `max` to `high`. Re-probe before narrowing this list.
models._motomoto_comment:
motomoto.lol - a New-API relay (X-New-Api-Version: v1.0.0-rc.31-motomoto.49).

DIRECT CONNECTIONS DO NOT WORK and they do not fail loudly: a direct HTTPS
request to any path answers `HTTP 200`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, and a
ZERO-LENGTH body. Measured 2026-09-24 - /, /v1, /v1/models, /v1/chat/
completions, /health, even a nonexistent path all answered the same way, so it
is the CDN, not the API. The same request through the local HTTP proxy returns
real JSON. Hence the provider-level `proxy` (same mechanism anyrouter uses).

WIRE: chat/completions only. /v1/responses and /v1/messages both answer
`Upstream service temporarily unavailable` (upstream_error / nil type) while
/v1/chat/completions works, so the gateway's chat bridge is the only path.

ID COLLISION: all four ids (codex-auto-review, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.5,
gpt-5.6-sol) are ALREADY registered against relaycat. They are therefore
exposed here under a `motomoto:` prefix. Do not overwrite the bare slugs -
that would silently reroute every existing caller to a different upstream.

CONCURRENCY: the operator reports a ceiling of one primary + one subagent
(2 concurrent requests). See the [agents] block in ~/.codex/config.toml.
models._justwoker_comment:
justwoker (api.justwoker.icu) is treated as an UNTRUSTED upstream.

Rationale: an independent packet scan of this provider reported counts per
field name, dominated by credential-shaped data - credentials 37657, API Key
22734, credential 8216, 令牌 6071, OpenAI Key 3917, 凭证 3191, 密钥 2546, JWT 2187,
密码 1458, dsn 1201, URL凭据 636, 私钥 469, AccessKey 378, SecretKey 204,
encryptionkey 184. A capture of a real request to it also showed the host
username, absolute workspace paths, the Windows build number, the timezone and
the shell name being sent verbatim, plus (because Codex reads files) whole API
keys inside tool_result blocks.

`egressGuard: true` therefore runs the FULL rule set from egress-guard.mjs
before the body is converted to the anthropic wire. That guard is FAIL-CLOSED:
if it throws, the request is refused with 500 rather than forwarded unredacted.
This differs from the agentrouter `filter`, which is deliberately fail-open
because it shapes content rather than protecting the host.

Wire: anthropic /v1/messages. The chat/completions face is Cloudflare-blocked
for this host (returns an HTML challenge page).
models._ovoapi_comment:
gpt-5.6-sol is the ONLY ovoapi id that serves. The other four ids the key's
group exposes (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol) answered 503 on
every probe, so they are not registered - see the provider _comment above.

PREFIXED because the bare slug gpt-5.6-sol is ALREADY served by relaycat. Do not
overwrite the bare slug; that would silently reroute every existing caller.
models._ovoapi_amz_comment:
The seven Claude ids served by the ovoapi-amz key (see that provider's _comment).

PREFIXED with ovoapi: because several bare slugs collide with existing routes:
claude-opus-4-8 is already served by justwoker, and claude-fable-5 / claude-opus-5
overlap the anyrouter ids. Overwriting a bare slug would silently reroute every
existing caller.

claude-opus-5 is the notable one: it was recorded as 'unavailable on every
provider we route' (see the _claude_comment at the end of this file) until this
key appeared. Verify before assuming that note is still accurate.

_claude_comment:
claude-opus-4-8 is served by justwoker over the anthropic-messages wire (see the anthropic bridge in bridge.mjs). It was briefly removed when only agentrouter offered it: agentrouter registers the claude ids on its anthropic-messages face only (messages=402 quota, responses=503, while a nonexistent model is 503 on both) and codex speaks only responses, so selecting them always failed. That is why the responses->messages bridge exists. claude-opus-5 WAS unavailable on every provider we route until 2026-09-30, when
the ovoapi-amz key appeared; it is now served as `ovoapi:claude-opus-5` (probed
three rounds, 200 every time, with working tool calls). The same key also brings
claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-5.5 and
claude-sonnet-5 - see the ovoapi-amz provider comment.
